evidence.intree_statement: Theorem Kan_Limit `(F : J ⟶ C) `{Lim : @Limit _ _ F} `{@RightKan _ _ (Erase J) C} : Lim ≅ Ran (Erase J) F ttt.

statement_record.book: For F : C ⟶ E and K : C ⟶ D: if for every d ∈ D the colimit of (K↓d) --Π^d--> C --F--> E exists in E, then those colimits define a functor Lan_K F : D ⟶ E which IS the left Kan extension of F along K, with unit η_c the colimit-cone leg at id_{Kc} ∈ K↓Kc; dually, if every limit of (d↓K) --Π_d--> C --F--> E exists, these define Ran_K F with counit ε_c the limit-cone leg at id_{Kc}.
statement_record.intree: Theorem Kan_Limit `(F : J ⟶ C) `{Lim : @Limit _ _ F} `{@RightKan _ _ (Erase J) C} : Lim ≅ Ran (Erase J) F ttt.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker, on four counts: (1) it is the single special case K := Erase J : J ⟶ 1 (where d↓K ≅ J for the unique object ttt), not a general K; (2) it ASSUMES a global RightKan already exists and merely compares its value with the limit — it does NOT construct a Kan extension out of the limits, which is the whole existence content of Theorem 6.2.1; (3) it is object-level only (an iso in C at the single object ttt): no comma category K↓d, no reindexing functor g_*, no functoriality of d ↦ Lan_K F(d), and no identification of the unit/counit with a (co)limit-cone leg; (4) only the right/limit side is proven — there is no Kan_Colimit dual.

gap: The general (co)limit formula is not formalized. Theory/Kan/Extension.v's own header (lines 74-79) states the position explicitly: 'Pointwise, the left extension at b is a colimit over the comma category F ↓ b and the right a limit over b ↓ F, equivalently Kelly's coend and end formulas ... the coend calculus of Structure/Coend.v ... is the in-tree machinery those formulas would rest on, a bridge not yet formalized.' Missing: the construction of Lan_K F / Ran_K F from pointwise (co)limits over K↓d / d↓K for a general K; its functoriality via the reindexing g_* ; the extraction of η/ε from the (co)limit cones; the verification of the universal property; and the entire colimit/left-hand half.
